analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 1 of a best-of-three, with No. 3 New England hosting No. 6 Philadelphia; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Marko Mitrovic's Revolution won both league meetings 2-1 but finished with two straight defeats, and Dor Turgeman (12 goals) and Ilay Feingold play for Israel in Hungary on 17 November, four days before kick-off. Philadelphia, under interim coach Ryan Richter according to MLSsoccer.com, ended a four-game winless run with a 4-1 win over Toronto led by Cavan and Quinn Sullivan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean a little lower: both meetings this season finished 2-1, New England scored once in their last two games, and Turgeman and Feingold will have had little time to recover from the Israel trip. Matt Turner, who played every minute of the season, gives New England a reliable last line in what should be a careful opener.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners, slightly more for Philadelphia. I found nothing on either side's set pieces or wide play that moves this, and Carles Gil's delivery keeps New England dangerous from dead balls, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. There is playoff history here (New England won in 2020, Philadelphia in 2023, both in Round One), but I found nothing on discipline or the referee that pushes it either way, so I stay close to the number.

shots.text: The site expects 26.4 shots with Philadelphia taking 16.9 of them, which looks heavy for an away team. Philadelphia did fire 19 at Toronto, but New England beat them twice this season and will not sit back at home in Game 1; I see a more even split and a slightly lower total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Turner made 140 saves this season, the second most in MLS, so New England do allow shots on goal, while Philadelphia's front line of Damiani and the Sullivans was sharp against Toronto. That supports the number, so I stay with it.
